title: skyBlip diagnostics capture record (v1)
description: ONE decoded record out of a diagnostics capture, as a host decoder reads it. Not schemas/diagnostics.v1.schema.json, which is the live status dump the companion link answers with: this is the recorded corpus a capture leaves behind, fetched over Bluetooth in the same base64 chunks the flight log uses and replayed on a laptop to re-derive the tuning constants (flight against taxi against ground, the gesture timings, the GNSS holdover, the dwell map). The firmware owns the layout (firmware/core/diag/): a 24-byte slot of 1 byte type, 1 byte flags, 2 bytes into_ms, 4 bytes at_s and 16 bytes of payload, every field little-endian and written one at a time. A capture is armed from the device's own diagnostics screen, lives in RAM only and dies at power off; a boot always comes up disarmed. The type tag is the corpus: a type is retired, never renumbered, because a capture outlives the firmware that wrote it. Every enum below is a wire format for the same reason: a payload stores the member's code and nothing else. The firmware writes those codes as explicit initialisers and each description below lists them, so a member added there takes the next free code instead of renumbering every capture behind it, and the order each enum is listed in here is the order of the codes, which is what the host decoder indexes by (firmware/core/diag/README.md says how both sides are pinned to this file). Every record carries type, at_s, into_ms, phase_valid and utc_dated; the rest of the keys belong to the type named at the front of each description and no record mixes two of them. Records a full ring had to refuse are never silent - the hole itself is a 'gap' record, in the place it happened, and a sector the ring recycled under a running capture is a 'gap' too, followed by a fresh 'boot' and 'config' so the surviving suffix still names its build. A 24-byte slot carries no CRC, so a torn slot cannot be told apart from telemetry: instead a session that stopped cleanly ends with an 'end' record, and a session the device reports as closed:false is one whose LAST record may be a half-written slot and must be dropped by the reader. A session reported truncated:true lost the sector it opened in, so it is a suffix renumbered from record zero and not a whole run.

type.description: What this record is about, from the type byte: boot=1, config=2, gnss=3, pps=4, burst=5, dwell=6, flight=7, power=8, baro=9, motion=10, contact=11, link=12, traffic=13, write=14, screen=15, gap=16, end=17, duty=18. Type 0 is not a record, so an all-zero slot decodes as nothing

at_s.description: The second this happened in: a UTC second when utc_dated is true, seconds since boot when it is false. A capture outlives a first fix and the records either side of one are dated differently, which is why the flag is per record

into_ms.description: Milliseconds into that second, measured against the PPS edge the clock latched (firmware/core/events/stamp.h). Meaningless unless phase_valid. Slot 1 reaches 200 ms past the second it opened in, so a burst can carry a phase above 999

phase_valid.description: into_ms was measured against a PPS edge rather than guessed at. False means the device held no lock, or the event and the edge were too far apart to be two views of one second

utc_dated.description: at_s is a real UTC second. False means seconds since boot, on a device that had not been told the date yet

capabilities.description: boot. The ports::Capability bitset the board came up with: bit 0 Rf, 1 Gnss, 2 Display, 3 Baro, 4 Buzzer, 5 Haptic, 6 Link, 7 Storage, 8 Dfu, 9 Contacts, 10 Battery, 11 DieTemperature, 12 HapticDriver, 13 Indicator, 14 Inclinometer. A shift is retired, never reused, for the reason a type tag is. A part that is not on this unit is a record type that never appears

fw_build.description: boot. Image version, build. CI stamps the run number here, so one corpus names one build

reset.description: boot. Why the device came up, as core/power/reset_reason.cpp spells it. A corpus that opens on WATCHDOG is a corpus whose first seconds are evidence. Codes: 0 UNKNOWN, 1 POWER ON, 2 RESET PIN, 3 BROWNOUT, 4 SOFT RESET, 5 WATCHDOG, 6 CPU LOCKUP, 7 CHARGER WAKE, 8 BUTTON WAKE, 9 DEBUGGER

image_state.description: boot. Whether the running image had been confirmed, was still on probation after an OTA, or had just been reverted by the bootloader. Codes: 0 confirmed, 1 probation, 2 reverted

addr.description: config: own 24-bit address. burst: the sender's, where the frame named one (addr_valid). traffic: the target's

addr_table.description: config. ADS-L address mapping table, issue 2 F.2.2. A constant 7 (OGN-Tracker) on this device

aircraft_type.description: config. ADS-L aircraft category in force

alarm_enabled.description: config. Whether the alarm was allowed to sound at all

metric.description: config. Units in force: true metric, false nautical. A display setting, recorded because it is what a pilot was reading

battery_offset_mv.description: config. The per-unit gauge trim every millivolt figure in this corpus has already been through

battery_trim_manual.description: config. That trim was measured by a person rather than learned off a charger's float plateau. A manual one outranks the learned one for good, so this is what says whether the trim_offset_mv on the power records would ever have been adopted

freq_trim_e1_ppm.description: config. The radio's centre-frequency trim, tenths of a ppm, applied to every dwell in this corpus

settings_version.description: config. The settings struct version the device was running, so a decoder knows which fields existed

tx_power_dbm.description: config. The power the transmitter was asked for, in dBm: the SX1262's SetTxParams argument, a nominal the part delivers within its own TXACC. 0 on a device with no radio, and on a capture older than the field

pa_rated_dbm.description: config. The output the PA configuration is rated for, in dBm: the row of SX1262 DS table 13-21 the executor writes. With tx_power_dbm it says which way the part was asked for its power, and a nominal conducted figure is the lower of the two. 0 on a device with no radio, and on a capture older than the field

nav_ms.description: gnss. How far into its own second the navigation solution landed, from the PPS edge. ADS-L G.1.16 refuses a solution older than 500 ms at the transmit instant, so this is the figure the whole transmit schedule stands on

resid_m.description: gnss. The extrapolation residual in metres: the model the transmitter applies, run over the interval that just elapsed and measured against the fix that closed it. Meaningless unless resid_valid, because 0 m is what a perfect prediction reports

resid_valid.description: gnss. There was a pair of consecutive fixes to measure the residual over

sats_in_view.description: gnss. Satellites the receiver reported seeing. Stops being refreshed once GSV is switched off, which the stage says

fix_mode.description: gnss. GSA field 2: 1 no fix, 2 is 2D, 3 is 3D

stage.description: gnss. Where acquisition had got to (core/gnss/acquisition.h). Codes: 0 silent, 1 blind, 2 solving, 3 fixed

stage_s.description: gnss. How long it had been in that stage, seconds, saturating

reject.description: gnss. Why the last solution was not accepted as a fix (core/gnss/validity.h). Codes: 0 NONE, 1 NO SOLUTION, 2 NO RMC, 3 NO GGA, 4 STALE, 5 NO DATE, 6 JUMP

fix_valid.description: gnss, flight. Own-ship held a usable fix at this instant

geoid_measured.description: gnss. The geoid separation behind the altitude came from the receiver rather than from a regional constant

tx_settled.description: gnss, flight. The fix had settled far enough for this device to be allowed to transmit

pps_locked.description: gnss. A PPS lock stood when the solution arrived

hdop_e2.description: gnss, flight. Horizontal dilution of precision in hundredths. Zero means the receiver did not report it, which is not the same as a good one

vdop_e2.description: gnss, flight. Vertical dilution in hundredths, GSA field 17. Zero on a 2D solution

interval_us.description: pps. Microseconds between this PPS edge and the one before it, on the clock the radio arms its deadlines against

error_us.description: pps. That interval less a nominal second, signed. The slot map's whole anchor is this number staying small

holdover_events.description: pps. Times at least one edge went missing (core/timing/timing_stats.h). kPpsHoldoverMs is 60 s of patience, and this is what says whether that is the right number

since_edge_ms.description: pps. How long ago the edge was, as the board reports it

locked.description: pps. The board considered the PPS locked

utc_valid.description: pps. A UTC second was known for that edge

verdict.description: burst. What happened to this burst, as firmware/core/radio/README.md spells the verdicts. Codes: 0 transmitted, 1 lost, 2 held, 3 unarmed, 4 received, 5 named, 6 bad_crc, 7 unframed, 8 miskeyed, 9 undecoded, 10 unsupported, 11 unattempted. named took code 5 on 2026-09-20 and pushed the six behind it up one: it is an ADS-L OGN diagnostics payload (type 66) carrying a registration, so a target on the table now has a name. A capture taken before that day has bad_crc at 5, which this table spells named, and nothing in the record says which of the two wrote it apart from the boot record's version. That is the renumbering the explicit codes exist to stop happening twice, and they are pinned on both sides (firmware/test/core/diag/test_diag_ordinals.cpp, scripts/test_blip.py)

band.description: burst, dwell. Which half of the second the single radio was in: M is the two 200 kHz traffic channels, O the ground station's HDR uplink. Codes: 0 M, 1 O

channel.description: burst. The M-band channel the dwell was tuned to, from the executor's own frequency: 0 is 868.2 MHz, 1 is 868.4. A receiver that never visits the second one hears half its neighbours

source.description: burst, traffic. Which path this came from: a direct ADS-L frame, a ground station's relay of one, an ALP-TAS frame, or own-ship. Codes: 0 adsl_direct, 1 adsl_uplink, 2 alptas, 3 own

len.description: burst. Bytes the radio reported for this burst

rssi_dbm.description: burst, traffic. The level it arrived at. Meaningless unless rssi_valid, and meaningless on a bench: two units on a desk read -6 to -17 dBm, which is a hundred dB over this modem's floor

rssi_valid.description: burst. The chip returned a level for this burst

addr_valid.description: burst. The frame named its sender. A refusal past the CRC still does, which is what makes a tape of refusals answerable

key_offset_s.description: burst. Seconds between the second an ALP-TAS sender keyed its frame on and ours, on a miskeyed verdict. The key stage moves every 16 s, so two seconds out means every frame from that emitter fails: the number is the diagnosis

tx_keyed_us.description: burst. Microseconds from the deadline the dwell was armed for to the executor issuing SetTx: this CPU's share of a burst

tx_span_us.description: burst. Microseconds from that same deadline to the executor reporting the burst sent: the keyed time plus the chip and the read-out. Meaningless unless tx_span_valid

tx_span_valid.description: burst. The executor reported a completion this span could be measured to

airborne.description: burst. Own-ship's flight state when the burst was written. Per record because G.1.16 transmits at 1 Hz in the air and 0.1 Hz on the ground, and a capture outlives a takeoff

callsign.description: burst. This burst carried a name rather than a position: own-ship's own, in slot 1's tail once every ten seconds (firmware/core/timing/README.md). The text itself is not recorded, because nine characters do not fit a 16-byte payload and the addr on this record is the key the name is filed under. A name heard from somebody else is the named verdict instead

state.description: dwell. Which stretch of the second the radio believed it was in (core/timing/slot.h). Codes: 0 uplink_rx_o, 1 switch_o_to_m, 2 slot0, 3 hop, 4 slot1, 5 switch_m_to_o

freq_hz.description: dwell. The centre frequency the dwell was armed on, trim included

start_ms.description: dwell. Where in the second the dwell opens, guards already subtracted

end_ms.description: dwell. Where it closes. Slot 1 closes at 1200, which is 200 ms into the next second

phase_ms.description: dwell, write. The phase in the second the decision was taken at, as the radio published it (core/timing/durable_write.h)

duty_permille.description: dwell. Parts per thousand of the hour's transmit allowance spent (EN 300 220-2 V3.3.1 Table 4 band M, 1%), which is the only rule that refuses a burst

noise_dbm.description: dwell. The measured noise floor. A diagnostic and nothing else: nothing on this device defers a burst to what it hears

refusal.description: dwell. Why nothing was transmitted in a second that allowed it: the hour's budget was spent, the executor refused the plan, own-ship was not settled enough to transmit, or this second was not its turn under G.1.16. Codes: 0 none, 1 over_budget, 2 unarmed, 3 unsettled, 4 off_schedule

tx_allowed.description: dwell. The slot map allowed own-ship to key the PA in this dwell

own_tx_dwell.description: dwell. This is the dwell own-ship places its own burst in

listen_only.description: dwell. The dwell was armed to receive and nothing else

armed.description: dwell. A dwell was actually armed at the radio when this was written

burst_armed.description: dwell. That dwell carried a burst whose outcome had not come back yet

speed_mm_s.description: flight. Ground speed in millimetres per second, the instruments' own resolution. The takeoff threshold is 12000 and the landing one 8000, and the gap between them is the hysteresis

climb_mm_s.description: flight: vertical rate in force when the state was decided. baro: the rate taken from this barometric sample

climb_valid.description: flight. Something had measured a vertical rate. ADS-L G.1.9 has an explicit unavailable code for when nothing had

alt_msl_m.description: flight. Geoid-referenced altitude in whole metres

declared.description: flight. What the flight machine decided on THIS evaluation. Written every time it runs, not only on transitions: a transition-only tape cannot say how close the machine came to deciding the other way, and that margin is the whole question when choosing a threshold. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 on_ground, 2 airborne

confirmed.description: flight. The same answer with the landing held back (core/flight/ground.h), which is what a permission gate reads. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 on_ground, 2 airborne

rolling.description: flight. Moving on the ground rather than stopped on it

cell_mv.description: power. The cell's terminal voltage in millivolts, after the per-unit trim

percent.description: power. State of charge on the cell's curve. Meaningless unless valid

level.description: power. What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 normal, 2 low, 3 cutoff

caution.description: power. The cell was past the knee: three consecutive samples under kCautionMv (3600), cleared by a cable or by a sample back above it. Not a level, because nothing acts on it - it is what the lamp winks about while every action is still allowed - and not a comparison a decoder can make on cell_mv, because the debounce and the charger are the decision

trim_offset_mv.description: power. The gauge trim this unit learned for itself off a charger holding its float voltage (core/power/trim.h). Meaningless unless trim_learned. Recorded rather than derived: cell_mv has already been through the trim in force, so the plateau the learner measured is nowhere in the corpus

trim_learned.description: power. A float plateau had been held long enough for the device to trim itself against it (kPlateauHoldMs, 120 s)

charge.description: power. Whether the die temperature allowed charging at all (LilyGO's 0-60 C window). Codes: 0 unknown, 1 ok, 2 too_cold, 3 too_hot

charging.description: power. The charger was holding the rail

external_power.description: power. Something was feeding the charger

valid.description: power. The gauge reading was believable at all: an unpopulated divider is not

die_dc.description: power. SoC die temperature in tenths of a degree Celsius, which reads above ambient. Meaningless unless die_valid

die_valid.description: power. A die reading existed. 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning, so absence is a flag and not a zero

supply_warnings.description: power. Times the nRF52840's power-failure comparator has fired, saturating. Any at all on a healthy cell is a supply problem

implausible.description: power. Gauge readings the 1800 mV sanity floor threw away, saturating

charge_warnings.description: power. Times charging was refused on temperature, saturating

pressure_mpa.description: baro. Static pressure in millipascals, the unit the driver hands over rather than the whole pascal it used to be truncated to

alt_mm.description: baro. Pressure altitude in millimetres, from the ICAO troposphere curve (core/flight/atmosphere.h)

temperature_dc.description: baro. Sensor temperature in tenths of a degree Celsius. Meaningless unless temperature_valid

temperature_valid.description: baro. The part reported a temperature with this sample

active.description: baro. The barometer was answering, so the vertical rate in force was its rather than the GNSS reference's

climb_adopted.description: baro. The rate from this sample is the one own-ship published

slip_mg.description: motion. Where the ball hangs, thousandths of g of lateral force as a fraction of the resultant. A ball position and never an accelerometer axis: the sign is the opposite of the force

slip_valid.description: motion. There was enough resultant to hang a ball from (200 mg)

normal_mg.description: motion. Load factor now, thousandths of g, positive up: 1000 in level flight

lateral_mg.description: motion. Lateral specific force now, thousandths of g

longitudinal_mg.description: motion. Longitudinal specific force now, thousandths of g

most_normal_mg.description: motion. The highest load factor held since the g-meter was reset

gload_valid.description: motion. The hub had answered inside kIndicatedStaleMs, so these are readings rather than history

fitted.description: motion. The sensor hub is on this unit. A plain T-Echo has none and writes no motion record at all; a Plus whose hub has not answered yet writes one with this true and gload_valid false

imu_error.description: motion. The hub's own error register, as the board read it

sensor_error.description: motion. The hub's per-sensor error byte

contact.description: contact. Which control moved. Codes: 0 button, 1 pad

down.description: contact. The edge was a press rather than a release

at_ms.description: contact. When the level changed, on the device's millisecond clock, not when the poll saw it. This is the instant the gesture constants are measured against

held_ms.description: contact. How long the level had held before this edge. On a release it is the length of the press, which is what kLongTouchMs (1000) and kLongPressMs are tuned against

gesture.description: contact. What the product made of the edge, as go::Gesture declares it: 0 none, 1 tap, 2 long touch, 3 press. A product code, carried so the corpus says what a press produced and not only what it was

action.description: link. The lifecycle event or the transfer this record is about. Nothing emits sent: the firmware's outbound frames are written where the claim this record carries cannot be read, and the code is held rather than retired so the others keep their numbers. Codes: 0 up, 1 down, 2 claim_taken, 3 claim_released, 4 received, 5 sent, 6 dropped

payload_bytes.description: link. The notification payload the central negotiated, which is the ATT MTU less three. The narrowest phone in the field carries 182

endpoint.description: link. Which characteristic the bytes were on. Codes: 0 config, 1 nmea, 2 log

frame_bytes.description: link. Bytes in the frame this record is about

holder.description: link. The session holding the claim, if any

claim_held.description: link. A claim stood at this instant. One central at a time gets to command the device

drops.description: link. Frames the link could not send, saturating: over the negotiated payload, refused by the controller, or left incomplete. Silence towards a phone is a fault worth a number

dist_m.description: traffic. Range to the target in metres, saturating. The advisory threshold is 3000

bearing_deg.description: traffic. Relative bearing, degrees clockwise from own-ship's track

rel_alt_m.description: traffic. The target's altitude less own-ship's, metres, positive above. The advisory window is 300 either way

closing_mps.description: traffic. Closing speed in metres per second, positive closing

alarm.description: traffic, screen. The alarm level decided for this target, and on a screen record the one standing: 0 none, 1 advisory

assessed.description: traffic. The geometry was complete enough to grade. False is a target on the table that no alarm could be formed about

dismissed.description: traffic. The pilot had silenced this one

in_formation.description: traffic. The target was being flown with rather than converged on

position_valid.description: traffic. The report carried a position at all. A relay carries no climb rate, no track and a quantised speed

tracked.description: traffic. Aircraft on the table after this update

placement.description: write. What the durable-write window decided: nothing to write, something to write but not now, now inside the window, or the bound is spent and it goes anyway. Forced is a fault and is counted as one. Codes: 0 idle, 1 hold, 2 place, 3 forced

kind.description: write. Which of the two durable writes: a convenience a pilot can make again, or the evidence of the flight that is ending. Codes: 0 settings, 1 flight_record

waited_ms.description: write. How long the oldest unwritten change had been waiting. kSettleMs is 750 and kMaxDeferMs is 3000, and this is the number both were chosen for

requests.description: write. Changes accepted since boot, saturating

writes.description: write. Flash writes they cost, saturating. The ratio is what the coalescing bought

forced.description: write. Writes that could not be placed inside their window, saturating

pending.description: write. A change was still unwritten when this was recorded

page.description: screen. Which page was on the glass, as the product's go::Page declares it: 0 radar, 1 nearby, 2 six-pack, 3 g-meter, 4 status, 5 sats, 6 radio log, 7 raw, 8 capture, 9 self-test. A product code and an ordinal, so it is read against the firmware version in the boot record and not against this list alone

mode.description: screen. 0 the page itself, 1 the menu over it, as go::Mode declares them

prompt.description: screen. The standing prompt waiting for a thumb, as comms::Pending declares it: 0 none, 1 set, 2 firmware upload, 3 apply, 4 recovery, 5 power off, 6 erase log, 7 GNSS cold start. A code this record does not own, read the way page is

since_ms.description: screen. How long that page had been up. ScreenService::kPresentFloorMs is 1000, and this is what says whether a pilot was ever shown less

powered.description: screen. The panel rails were up. A parked device holds its last image with them down

holding.description: screen. A refresh was being held back on die temperature: Good Display rates the glass 0 to 50 C

dropped.description: gap: records the ring had to refuse, right here. Silent loss in a corpus you are going to tune constants from is poison, so the hole is a record like any other. end: records the ring refused over the whole session

span_ms.description: gap. Milliseconds from the first refused record to the last, so a reader knows how much time the hole covers and not only how many records

total.description: gap. Records refused since the capture was armed, this hole included

capacity.description: gap. Slots the RAM ring holds, so a reader can tell a burst of records from a writer that stopped keeping up

records.description: end. Records the session wrote before this marker, as the device counted them

panel_partial_refreshes.description: duty. Panel refreshes the device asked for on the partial waveform, low 16 bits of a 32-bit counter. The SSD1681 driver promotes the first one after a boot, a busy timeout or an aborted refresh to a full, and that promotion is not counted. Every duty field wraps rather than saturating, because a reader takes the difference between two records and unsigned subtraction crosses a wrap correctly: the emitting cadence is bounded at 60 s (firmware/core/diag/payload.h kDutyMaxPeriodMs) so one interval's delta cannot reach 65536. A 16-bit millisecond field wraps every 65.5 s, so a reader must not subtract two duty records across a gap record, a boot record, a session boundary, a missing or unreadable record index, two instants dated differently (one UTC, one since boot), or a pair further apart than kDutyMaxPeriodMs: that interval is dropped, never estimated. A capture that parks writes one last power record then one last duty record, off the cadence, before its end record

panel_full_refreshes.description: duty. Panel refreshes asked for on the full waveform, the expensive ones: a full clear costs seconds of the e-paper controller and several times the charge of a partial. Wraps, like every duty field

backlight_ms.description: duty. Milliseconds the backlight has been lit. Wraps, like every duty field

rx_armed_ms.description: duty. Milliseconds the radio has been armed to receive, which is most of the second the dwell map fills. Wraps, like every duty field

tx_keyed_ms.description: duty. Milliseconds the PA has been keyed, the whole of it inside the 1% band M allowance. Wraps, like every duty field

ble_connected_ms.description: duty. Milliseconds a central has been connected, advertising excluded. Wraps, like every duty field

annunciator_ms.description: duty. Milliseconds the buzzer and the haptic have been driven, summed: the two are one consumer at this resolution. Wraps, like every duty field
